A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Proxy Compression for Language Modeling. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and consolidated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, code-generation results, cross-representation transfer probes, compressor ablations, and robustness evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds natural-language results, prompt-boundary evaluations, and a late-finetuning comparison.

M1.justification: The mixed-representation training procedure, compressors, format sentinels, pairing warmup, mixing schedule, and raw-byte inference remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of packing and compressor state do not establish a changed implementation or algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix D.12 extends the previously code-focused evaluation to Nemotron-CLIMB training and nine natural-language benchmarks: ARC-c, ARC-e, BoolQ, CSQA, HellaSwag, OBQA, PIQA, SIQA, and WinoGrande. This substantially broadens domain and task coverage while retaining the original code experiments.

E2.justification: Appendix D.12 adds late raw-byte finetuning of a tokenizer-only checkpoint as an evaluated alternative to mixed-representation pretraining. Existing code comparators remain unchanged; the OpenCoder architecture comparison highlighted in v2's setup already appeared in v1's Appendix C.1 and Figure 10.

E3.justification: New protocols include 1.5B natural-language runs with 50K steps, 0.5M symbols per batch, and OLMES-based accuracy evaluation; a 7B boundary test applying eight suffixes plus a baseline to 164 HumanEval prompts; and a 5K-step late-finetuning control. Existing code-training and decoding settings remain unchanged, and pass@10 was already defined in v1.

E4.justification: Appendix D.11 adds targeted prompt-boundary sensitivity testing beyond the retained ReCode analyses. Appendix D.12 also tests whether late byte finetuning can substitute for mixed pretraining. These supplement the existing compressor, pairing, mixing, masking, and representation analyses.

E5.justification: Table 15 newly summarizes performance with means and standard deviations across nine prompt variants, including HumanEval deviations of 0.88 for the tokenizer proxy and 14.05 for the tokenizer baseline. These measure perturbation sensitivity, not repeated-training uncertainty; no new seed counts or confidence intervals are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds cross-scale pass@10 results (Table 9), boundary results (Table 15), natural-language scores (Table 16: average accuracy 50.3 for the proxy, 48.2 for bytes, and 51.5 for tokenization), and finetuning outcomes. Main Tables 1–4 remain unchanged. Figure 3's tokenizer endpoint changes from approximately 27.4% to 29.3%, matching Table 1. Figure 13 revises byte-level format RP from 0.20 to 0.29 and token-inference proxy RP from 0.29 to 0.31, while restoring the missing neural-proxy bar. These establish reporting changes, not evidence of reruns.

T1.justification: The compression-ratio derivations in Appendix A, compressor definitions, and robustness formulas remain mathematically unchanged. Corrected notation and explanatory prose do not introduce new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain efficient mixed-representation training, scalable transfer to raw bytes, and retained robustness without architectural changes. The abstract and conclusion now say 'match or surpass' rather than 'match or rival,' but v1's introduction already made the surpassing claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about learning-rate confounds in matched-data comparisons, confounded explanations for pairing-schedule differences, and architecture-dependent byte-decoding costs. It narrows the main-text all-scales performance statement and updates beyond-code applicability from untested to initially supported, while leaving larger-scale, multilingual, and mixed-domain validation open.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly explains compression before packing, document-local compressor state, window resets, and suffix truncation. v2 also specifies budgets and perturbation construction for the added experiments and corrects the gzip API notation. These are documentation additions; the code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Diao et al. on Nemotron-CLIMB and Gu et al. on OLMES to support the natural-language experiments. The related-work argument and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; publication and URL updates for existing references are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted paragraph rewrites, grammar repairs, and terminology corrections, including clarifying that the 10% raw-data fraction concerns samples rather than tokens. It expands documentation, adds Appendices D.11–D.12, and updates the publication header while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9, 15, and 16, consolidates v1's Figures 19–22 into Figure 19(a–d), repairs Figure 13's incomplete bar display, and adjusts placements, captions, and decimal formatting. The consolidated plots preserve the earlier analyses, and the overall visual format remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the paper with initial evidence beyond code, a direct test of motivating prompt-boundary artifacts, and a late-finetuning control. Corrections to Figures 3 and 13 improve consistency, while new qualifications make efficiency and mechanism interpretations more careful. These are clear but bounded gains: natural-language validation remains limited to 1.5B models, and broader generalization remains unresolved.
